calibrated_with.shape_complementarity: VALIDATED for implementation (BIO Scientist, 2026-10-20, in-image, $0.00, nothing submitted). Recomputed under shape-complementarity==0.2.0 / sc-rs befcc6c on n=1,028 Nipah glycoprotein-G complexes: Pearson r=0.999959, Spearman rho=0.999945, mean |delta| 2.9e-4 SC units, 100% within +/-0.01, no signed offset. ROC-AUC vs measured BLI binding (100 binders/928 non-binders): ours 0.6873 [95% boot CI 0.6224,0.7480] vs Adaptyv column 0.6878 [0.6229,0.7479]; paired dAUC -0.00044 [-0.00109,+0.00016] (straddles zero, 4 orders narrower than the AUC CI). So shape-complementarity==0.2.0 REPRODUCES Adaptyv's quantity to float noise -> the 0.688 transfer STANDS and SC keeps its rank_average weight unchanged. STILL transferred ACROSS TARGET CLASS: Proteinbase has no pMHC, so the threshold is validated for implementation only, not for pMHC; campaign one remains its own calibration experiment. Caveat: Adaptyv's own SC parameters are an INFERENCE (proteinbase_README.md defines no params for the shape_complimentarity column); 'sc-rs at defaults' is read off 1,028 complexes agreeing to 2.9e-4, not off a spec, and only on the Nipah subset (1,028 of 4,273 PPIs). Report: /workspace/wetware/binder-design/v3/sc-recompute-2026-10-20.md (sha256 3ed7ea12f000...90c8cdf0).
calibrated_with.metric_code_reuse: Adaptyv competition_metrics is Apache-2.0 but computes only iPTM, pae_interaction, ESM2 PLL and a rank-average - no SC/SASA/H-bond/dG code, so only the pae_interaction definition and the rank-average convention are reusable

descriptors.calibration_note: Every roc_auc above is a threshold TRANSFERRED from Adaptyv's own columns, not computed under our stack. calibrated_with names the producing implementation per descriptor so a reproducible pin is never mistaken for a calibrated number. descriptors.interface_definition_note: SC's interface is NOT our interface: sc-rs uses a native Connolly surface with nearest-neighbour dot pairing, while our ifd_* descriptors use a 5.0 A residue contact cutoff and a 1.4 A SASA probe. SC and the other rank-average descriptors are scoring interfaces defined two different ways. Defensible, but recorded so it is not discovered later.
descriptors.data_join_caveat: id is NOT unique in tidy.parquet (204 dupes: same designs counter-screened vs human serum albumin). A naive merge on id gives ~1,129 rows and silently mixes an off-target row into the on-target cohort. Filter target=='nipah-glycoprotein-g' first and assert one-to-one.

modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.verdict_before_fix: DOES NOT FUNCTION against the pinned digest, for three INDEPENDENT and individually fatal reasons, each proved live in-image.
modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.defect_1_worker_absent: python -m bindi.ipsae raises ModuleNotFoundError in the bare image. Fixed by the wheel layer (see layer2_execution_pin).
modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.defect_2_default_chains: DEFAULT_CHAINS was 'A:275,B:99,C:9' - the three TARGET chains only, omitting the binder, whose length varies per design. --chains is a STRICT ASSERTION against the CIF, not a repartitioning override: bindi._resolve_chain_specs requires every named chain to exist with the EXACT residue count, and validate_token_alignment additionally requires the lengths to sum to the PAE token count. Proof: 'A:5,B:5' sums correctly to 10 tokens and STILL raises (chain A is 6 residues in the CIF). So the constant was structurally guaranteed to raise TokenAlignmentError on EVERY real design. Fixed: DEFAULT_CHAINS = '' so the worker derives chains from the CIF, which is authoritative.
modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.defect_3_stdout_mapping: score_one read raw['ipsae'], raw['min_ipsae'], raw.get('ipsae_ab'/'ipsae_a_b'), raw.get('ipsae_ba'/'ipsae_b_a'), raw.get('complex_plddt'/'complex_iplddt'). NONE of those top-level keys exist - the worker's JSON is nested. Replayed against real worker output it raised KeyError: 'ipsae'. The reader itself was correct (the worker does json.dump to stdout and writes no metrics file); the consuming mapping was wrong. Fixed to raw['pairs'][pair]['min_ipsae'], ['ipsae_<A>_to_<B>'], raw['plddt']['complex_plddt'].
modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.defect_3b_pair_selection: pairs holds ONE ENTRY PER CHAIN PAIR (a 3-chain fixture returned A|B, A|C, B|C; a real 4-chain complex yields 6), so a flat 'ipsae' is undefined until an interface is named. Fixed by BINDER_CHAIN and _select_pair, which takes the WEAKEST binder-containing pair, matching the worker's conservative min(A->B, B->A).
modal_functions_defects_found_and_fixed_.unverified_constant: BINDER_CHAIN = 'D' comes from the file's own comment, NOT from a real artifact (none exists yet). If Boltz letters the binder differently, _select_pair fails loudly with the chains it did see rather than scoring the wrong interface - but this constant MUST be checked against the first real CIF before any layer-2 result is trusted.

image.digest_is_content_address: same digest as the pinned ghcr image elsewhere in this file; MUST NOT be replaced by a tag
image.private_registry_auth: ghcr.io is private -> Modal Secret 'ghcr-wetware-ro' holding REGISTRY_USERNAME + REGISTRY_PASSWORD (a GitHub token with read:packages). Fine-grained tokens expose Packages only when the org allows it, so a classic token with read:packages is the reliable form. Per https://modal.com/docs/guide/private-registries.
image.add_python: NOT used - the fleet-env image already has python+pip on PATH
image.content_address_effect: Modal pulls the base by digest and does not rebuild or mutate the base layers, so the scientific env (numpy==2.4.6, gemmi==0.7.5, shape-complementarity==0.2.0, biopython) is byte-identical to the ghcr image; Modal only APPENDS its client-runtime layer. The ghcr digest stays the pinned base and the content address. OD-8 is NOT reopened. The Modal Image object-id differs from the ghcr digest - that is the appended layer, not a change to the base.
image.can_use_unmodified: YES as-is, provided the image is linux/amd64 and its ENTRYPOINT execs its args (or has none). If the ghcr ENTRYPOINT does not exec "$@", override with Image.entrypoint([...]). This is the single item to confirm against the image.

score_one.returns: ipsae, min_ipsae (both chain orderings when reported), complex_plddt, plddt.present - all NON-GATING, recorded only. Gating stays iptm and plddt.
score_one.guard: TokenAlignmentError raised in-image is re-raised, never swallowed
score_one.cpu: 1.0 physical core - ipSAE is O(n^2) numpy on a ~256x256 PAE plus one gemmi parse, sub-second to low-seconds, single-threaded; more cores buy nothing, and 1.0 stops the gemmi parse being throttled under the 0.125 default
score_one.memory_mib: 2048 - arrays are tiny (~0.26 MiB); the footprint is importing numpy+scipy+gemmi+biopython. 2 GiB gives headroom with an OOM backstop; the 128 MiB default risks OOM on import alone
score_one.timeout_s: 300 - a design scores in seconds; 300 s is a loud bound that trips a hang rather than tolerating it. Image pull and cold start are not counted against it
score_one.retries: 0 - scoring is a pure deterministic function of (cif, pae); every failure mode here (TokenAlignmentError, bad CIF, absent pLDDT) is deterministic and recurs identically, so input-retries only delay the loud failure. Container-crash reschedule (OOM, host loss) is Modal's separate mechanism, orthogonal to input retries
score_one.max_containers: 10 - one per design; bounds the concurrent billable core-second burst

fan_out.modal_api: Function.starmap(iterable_of_tuples) - each tuple unpacked into score_one's positional args

entrypoint.modal_api: @app.local_entrypoint() main() reads ART artifacts, starmaps, and writes ONE canonical-JSON results file (sort_keys, compact separators, sorted by design_id) so the output and its hash are deterministic regardless of completion order

cost_surface.where_in_graph: L2 is downstream of the APPR approve edge (CFG->APPR->L1A->L1B->ART->L2), so it only runs on the approve path and already inherits the human gate; no new gate added
cost_surface.hard_ceiling: billable core-seconds <= max_containers * timeout * cpu = 10 * 300 * 1.0 = 3000 per 10-design run; memory billed at max(request, usage)
cost_surface.rate_not_quoted: Modal's $/core-second is on its pricing page, NOT fetched this session, so no dollar figure is asserted here; at any plausible rate 3000 core-seconds is cents, negligible beside the $15 Boltz spend but NOT zero
cost_surface.rule: the Modal layer-2 projection MUST be added to costs.spent_to_date_usd and included in the same pre-APPR cost projection as the Boltz spend; the run aborts if (Boltz + Modal projected) > spend_cap_usd = 15.00. The cap and on_deny = HALT are unchanged.
cost_surface.optional_volume_cut: a modal.Volume was deliberately NOT used: the 10 artifacts are tiny and already mirrored off-API to repo and box, so a Volume adds a durability surface that buys nothing here
